full_judgment:
5. On 1.8.87 a First Information Report was lodged by Mr. Md. Shahadat Hossain, ASP, Bureau of Ant-Corruption, Bangladesh Dhaka, against the present two petitioners and another under sections 420/367/471/ 406/109 of the Penal Code alleging, inter alia, that a sugar mill, namely Morang Sugar Mills Ltd. was established in Tumulia Union under Police Station Rupganj, District Narayanganj and its owner was childless. On partition of India in 1947 the owner of the mill took the machineries of the mill to Nepal by a ship through waterways. Since 1947 till 1972, that is, for about 26 years nobody claimed this property of the said Morang Sugar Mills Ltd. here and as such the property was first treated as evacuee property and subsequently it was treated as vested property. 

 6. In 1976 one Bangu Miah of Kaliganj declared that the working Director of the said Mill Mr. Jodhya Bahadur Shrestha, by a letter dated 9.6.72, appointed him as Caretaker of the said mill and since that date he had been looking after and taking care of the aforesaid mill. In the year 1976 the Sub-Divisional Officer, Narayanganj, started VP Case No.1 of 1976 and through that case 2157 acres of land of the said mill was settled with the local people, namely, Mr. Abdur Rouf and 9 others on temporary basis. The said Bangu Miah filed an application in the aforesaid VP Case for release of this said property from the list of the vested property. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.) sent all the papers and materials to Mr. Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman, Advocate, and Legal Adviser for vested and non-resident property for his opinion as to whether the said property fell in the category of vested and non-resident property of abandoned property. The learned Advocate Mr. Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman gave his opinion that the property in question was neither vested property nor abandoned property. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Dhaka, sent all the papers and documents including the opinion of the Advocate Mr. Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman to the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms with recommendation for releasing the said property from the list of the vested and non-resident property. 

 7. In the meantime, Bangu Miah died. Further, it appears that one Mr. Dhruba Kumar Thapa claiming himself as General Manager of the said Morang Sugar Mills Ltd. appointed accused Abdur Rahman, the son-in-law of Bangu Miah, as the caretaker of the property of the aforesaid mill by a letter dated 31.12.80. On receiving the papers and documents including the legal opinion from the Additional Deputy Commissioner(Rev.), Dhaka, the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reform, by an order as contained in the Memo, No. 3381/VP-92-78 dated 27.11.80, released the property from the list of vested and non-resident property in favour of the aforesaid mill Further, it appears that the Board of Directors of Morang Sugar Mills Ltd, Nepal, by a resolution dated 2.6.85 empowered Mr. Jodhya Bahadur Shrestha, a Director, to look after and take all steps for management of the property of the aforesaid mills. It is alleged that without any authority the said Director Mr. Jodhya Bahadur Shrestha on 9.6.72 appointed Bangu Miah as care-taker of the said property. It is further alleged that without any authority the said Director Mr. Jodhya Shrestha by a letter dated 20.12.82 appointed Mr. Abdus Samad, Bar-at-Law, as an Attorney executing a general power of attorney in his favour. After obtaining the aforesaid power of attorney Mr. Abdus Samad was looking after the above property of the mill and made all arrangements for selling the property of the mill to one, Nazrul Islam. Said Mr. Jodhya Bahadur Shrestha entered into an agreement with Mr. Nazrul Islam on 25.6.86 by a registered deed of agreement at a price of Taka 11,00.000 and the purchaser had given Taka 6,50,000.00 as advance to the seller. Out of that amount of Taka 6,50,000.00 the seller took Taka 2,68,000.00 and Taka 3,82,000.00 was deposited to Mr. Abdus Samad, the Attorney of the mill. As per agreement some of the movable properties of the mill were taken by Mr. Nazrul Islam from the mill site. In accordance with the President's Order No 26 of 1972 all the properties of Morang Sugar Mills Ltd. were treated as vested and abandoned property and the real owner of the properties is the Government of Bangladesh. On the above allegations the accused are liable for creating forged and false documents for selling the vested and abandoned properties of the Government at an amount of Taka 11,00,000.00 although the real value of the properties would be at Taka 50,00,000.00. On the above allegations against the two petitioners and another the case under sections 402/467/471/406/109 of the Penal Code was instituted. 

 8. On behalf of the accused-petitioners it is stated that a First Information Report was lodged under sections 420/467/471/406/109 of the Penal Code by an Assistant Superintendent of Police, Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Bangladesh, Dhaka, with Rupganj Police Station against the petitioners and another for alleged collusive sale of non-resident/ vested/abandoned properties of Morang Sugar Mills Ltd. of Nepal situated at Shome Bazar, Police Station Rupganj, District Narayanganj, Bangladesh. This case was started by the Anti-Corruption Department on 1.8.87. On 28.1.88 Inquiry Officer (IO) prayed for extension of time for 30 days for filing the police report. No police report was submitted on 28.2.88, 15.3.88, 17.4.88, 7.5.88, 30.5.88 and 12.6.88, though the Court fixed all the above dates for filing police report. On 12.6.88 the Magistrate did not receive any police report from the Investigating Officer and the learned Magistrate stopped further proceeding of the case on 12.6.88 as the Investigating Officer could not submit any report against the accused person within the statutory period as per provision of section 167(5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. On 26.7.89 the Upazila Magistrate, Rupganj, by his order received the aforesaid criminal case on the basis of the letter issued by Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Bangladesh, Dhaka On 25.9.89 charge-sheet No. 77 dated 20.9.89 under sections 420/467/471/406/109 of the Penal Code was submitted in the Court of the Upazila Magistrate, Rupganj, by Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Bangladesh, Dhaka, against the two petitioners, namely, Mr. Md. Abdus Samad and Mr. Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman. On 24.10.89 the charge-sheet was accepted by the Magistrate. 

 9. It is further stated that the aforesaid company, namely, M/s Morang Sugar Mills Ltd. was a private company of Nepal who had possessed as absolute owner of the property in question. Some unauthorised occupants occupied a portion of the property of the mill forcibly and unauthorisedly during liberation war of 1971 and on their representation the Government granted temporary lease with them for some particular area of the land. After coming to know of the aforesaid fact of occupation of the mill's property by some unauthorised persons an application was filed before the authority and VP Case No 1 of 1976 was instituted and on behalf of the mill the prayer was made to the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms for releasing the aforesaid property in favour of the mill. On 26.11.78 the aforesaid Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms obtained necessary reports of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Dhaka, vide Memo No. 118 dated 16.1.78 and legal opinion from the then VP Lawyer. On 28.9.80 the aforesaid VP Case was heard by the Ministry which considered the period for the years 1978 to 1980. After hearing the company, the lessees and illegal occupants, the said Ministry released the property by its Memo. No. 3381-VP-92/78 dated 28.11.80 in favour of the Company M/s Morang Sugar Mills Ltd. Thereafter possession of the property was handed over to the Caretaker of the company by the CO (Rev.) and the OC Rupganj Police Station on 12.3.81 under direction of the Ministry. 

 10. After release of the property the company decided to dispose of the said property and an advertisement was made in the newspapers. One M/s Nazrul Enterprise of Chasara, Narayanganj, became the highest bidder who offered Taka eleven lakh. On 20.12.82 a general power of attorney was executed by the company in favour of the petitioner Mr. Abdus Samad which was duly attested by the Bangladesh Embassy in Nepal. Mr. Abdus Samad was authorised to manage, supervise, control, evict the unauthorised and illegal occupants and to do all other thing or things as necessary for management of the said property as per terms of the power of attorney. From the year 1983 to 1985 steps were taken to evict the unauthorised and illegal occupants from the said property who unauthorisedly entered into premises in the year 1971. Mr Mir Mosharraf Hossain, Advocate was one of the unauthorised occupants and he was also asked to vacate the premises. On 5.6.85 an agreement for sale was executed by the aforesaid Nepali company and M/s. Nazrul Enterprise for the sale of the said property and a sum of Taka five lakh was paid to Mr. JB Shrestha, the then working Director of the company as advance. But subsequently the agreement was cancelled by the purchaser on 7.7.85 as the company failed to evict the unauthorised occupants from the premises. 

 11. On coming to know about the sale of the property the illegal occupants including the said Advocate Mir Mosharraf Hossain made several false, fictitious and baseless complaints to the President's Secretariat, Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Deputy Commissioner, Narayanganj and other places against the sale of the property. On the basis of those complaints the President's Secretariat, that is, Cabinet Division, directed the Deputy Commissioner, Narayanganj, to inquire and report. Accordingly, the Deputy Commissioner started proceeding. On the instruction of the Deputy Commissioner the inquiry was held by UNO Rupganj, GP Narayanganj, Revenue Deputy Collector, Narayanganj, into the matter and all gave opinion that the property in question was neither vested property nor abandoned property. The President's Secretariat, Cabinet Division, also directed the Secretary of Ministry of Industries by a letter dated 25.10.86 to inquire into the matter of Morang Sugar Mill's property at Rupganj and report and the said Ministry also found that the property of Morang Sugar Mills Ltd. is neither vested nor abandoned nor a nationalised property and accordingly, the President's Secretariat was informed by a letter dated 20.12.86. The Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Bangladesh, on the basis of the complaint made to it by the illegal occupants made inquiry and found the allegation totally false, fictitious and baseless and recommended for taking action against those illegal occupants of the premises. A fresh agreement for sale was executed on 25.6.86 by the company represented by Mr. JB Shrestha, the authorised Director of the company, supported by resolution of the Board of Directors of the company dated 2.6.85 and the said purchaser company M/s. Nazrul Enterprise. At the time of agreement dated 2.6.85 Mr. MP Pandel, Second Secretary of Royal Embassy of Nepal was present who identified and attested the signature of the said Director Mr. JB Shrestha at the Nepal Embassy. The said Director Mr. JB Shrestha received Taka five lakh on behalf of the vendor company as earnest money from the buyer. In addition to that an amount of Taka 1,50,000.00 was deposited to the then Gulshan Branch of BCCI Bank through the Royal Embassy of Nepal on 25.6.86. The said Director then went to the site at Rupganj along with the purchaser and handed over the possession to the purchaser as per said agreement for sale. On 23.12.86 the petitioner Mr. Abdus Samad applied to Bangladesh Bank through Grindlays Bank, Dilkusha Branch, Dhaka, for permission to deposit Taka 3,82,000.00 in the Blocked Account paid to the petitioner by the aforesaid Director of the vendor-company for remittance of the said money to the company in Nepal and the money was deposited as such on 5.1.87 in the Bank and the entire sum is still lying there. On 31.3.87 again the illegal and unauthorised occupants of premises lodged a false complaint against the petitioners to the Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Bangladesh, Dhaka and on that complaint the First Information Report was lodged by the Anti-Corruption Officer against the present petitioners and another on 1.8.87 as stated above. On 12.6.88 when the police report could not be submitted within the stipulated period, the proceedings were stopped under section 167(5) of the Code of Criminal Procedure. On 20.6.89 the case was revised by the Magistrate at the instance of the Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Bangladesh, Dhaka and on 25.9.89 charge-sheet No.77 dated 20.9.89 under sections 420/467/471/406/109 of the Penal Code was submitted before the Upazila Magistrate, Rupganj by the Bureau of Anti-Corruption against the present petitioners Mr. Abdus Samad and Mr. Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman. 

 14. Subsequently the case was revived on 26.7.89 by the learned Magistrate in pursuance of Memo No.8000 dated 26.7.89 and Memo No.2803 dated. 28.6.89. The learned Advocate submits that as per provision of section 167 (7A) the case was required to be revived on the order of the District Magistrate within six months from the date of stopping the proceedings. From the record itself it appears that the proceeding was stopped on 12.6.88, but it was revived on 26.7.89. So, it was revived long after the period fixed by the provisions of law, that is within six months from the date of stopping the proceedings. The learned Advocate submits that since the revival of the proceedings is illegal, the proceedings itself as well as all other subsequent actions taken after 29.9.87 and 12.6.88 are illegal and without jurisdiction. We find substance in the above contentions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners. So, on this count this Rule issued in Criminal Revision No. 273 of 1989 should be made absolute and the order dated 26.7.89 is liable to be declared illegal. Learned Advocate further submits that even if it is presumed that the proceeding was revived under the law, even then this proceeding is liable to be quashed in view of the fact that these two present petitioners performed their duties as lawyers in connection with releasing of the property and selling of the same. He submits that the property in question cannot be treated either as vested or abandoned property in view of the fact that the property admittedly belonged to a Nepali company. He further submits that since the Government after detailed inquiry into the matter released the property in favour of the Nepali company and that order of release still stands valid, in the eye of law the properties in question still belong to the Nepali company and, as such, the Anti-Corruption Department had nothing to do with the selling of the properties by the Director of the company. 

 15. With regard to the petitioner Mr. Md. Abdus Samad, it is submitted that as lawyer he took steps for releasing the property in favour of the Nepali company being authorised by the Director of the company and subsequently he was appointed as Attorney by virtue of a registered power of attorney of the company. Further, he submits that even in the deed of agreement which was made between the Nepali company and M/s. Nazrul Enterprise in the Nepali Embassy, petitioner Abdus Samad was not a witness to that document. Whether that document is legal or illegal, forged or fabricated, the petitioner Mr. Abdus Samad had got nothing to do with that document. He further submits that it is curious that neither the Director of the Nepali company nor the purchaser Mr. Nazrul Islam was made an accused in the instant proceeding. So, the ingredients of sections 420/467/471/406/109 of the Penal Code are totally absent in the case of the petitioner Mr. Md. Abdus Samad. We find full substance in the above contentions of the learned Advocate. We have gone through the First Information Report, the charge-sheet and all other connected papers and documents available on record and from the same we find that the ingredients of the aforesaid sections are totally absent in the whole case against Mr. Abdus Samad and, as such, no proceedings should lie against him. 

 16. As regards the petitioner Mr. Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman, it appears to us from the record that at the relevant time he was a legal Adviser of the vested and non-resident property. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), Dhaka, placed all the papers and materials before him and after considering the papers and documents he simply expressed his opinion that the property in question cannot be treated as vested property or abandoned property in view of the fact that the property belonged to a Nepali company. On the basis of the opinion given by the legal Adviser, Advocate Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman, and all other relevant papers and documents, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev.), became satisfied and recommended for release of the aforesaid property from the list of vested property to the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms of the Government of Bangladesh. Thereafter, the matter was inquired into by the Ministry and after considering the relevant papers and documents the Ministry itself became satisfied that the property in question is not a vested or abandoned property and, as such, the Ministry passed an order releasing the same to the Nepali company. It further appears that several complaints were made against this property of the aforesaid company and different organs of the Government inquired into the same. But all the agencies of the Government submitted favourable reports in favour of releasing the same. Being a Legal Adviser Mr. Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman gave his opinion for releasing the property in favour of the Nepali company and we fail to understand how a case under the aforesaid sections will lie against a legal adviser who had not done anything with regard to execution of the deed of agreement for sale. On the face of the record it appears that the ingredients of the aforesaid section of the Penal Code are totally absent in respect of the Advocate Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman. As such, this proceeding cannot lie against him. In our opinion, the proceeding against Mr. Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman is absolutely baseess and, as such, liable to be quashed. In the result the Rule issued in Criminal Revision No. 273 of 1989 at the instance of petitioner Mr. Md. Abdus Samad is made absolute and the impugned order dated 26.7.89 passed in GR Case No.108 of 1987 arising out of Rupganj Police Station Case No.1 of 1987 is hereby set aside. 

 19. The matter was investigated by different agencies of the Government available from the records. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Rev) Narayanganj, after inquiring into the matter submitted a report to the Government recommending for release and the concerned Ministry after examining the materials on record in fact released the property in favour of the Nepali company and that release order still stands valid and the Government did not in any way claim the aforesaid property. We do not find any reason for the Bureau of Anti-Corruption to start a case against the present two petitioners who being lawyers acted and performed their duties in the case. Mr. Md. Abdus Samad was simply appointed as Attorney by virtue of a general power of attorney and he looked after the property on behalf of the Nepali company. We fail to understand as to how the Bureau of Anti-Corruption had started such a frivolous case against the present two petitioners. Further, it is funny to see that allegation of forgeddeed was made against the present two petitioners while the seller and the purchaser were not made parties in such a criminal case. On the basis of the materials on record we find that the Bureau of Anti-Corruption had filed the instant case without any basis at all and we also find that with some malafide motive the instant case was filed against the present two petitioners. 

 21. The person who lodged the First Information Report had no knowledge about the geographical position of Nepal. He stated that the original owner of this mill just before partition of India in 1947 took all the machineries of the said mill by a ship and went to Nepal through waterways. The owner of the mill had no occasion to take all the machineries to the mill and go to Nepal by waterways by ship inasmuch as Nepal is situated just near the Himalayas and it is a land-locked country. This shows that somehow the officer who lodged the First Information Report created and manufactured this story against the present two petitioners only to harass them and for no other reason. The present petitioners are two Advocates of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh and they are respectable persons. They performed their duties and obligations as lawyers and they had no other connection with the properties of the Nepali company in question in Bangladesh. By instituting this frivolous and baseless case they are being simply harassed for no fault of their own. As such, the relevant officers are liable to be punished for instituting a frivolous, baseless and vexatious case against the present two petitioners. 

 Let a copy of this judgment be sent to the Secretary, Ministry of Home Affairs, and Government of Bangladesh as well as to the Inspector General of Police, Bangladesh. They are directed to take appropriate legal action against Mr. Md. Shahadat Hossain, the then ASP, Anti-Corruption Officer, Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Bangladesh, Dhaka, who lodged the First Information Report on 1.8.82 and Mr. Abdul Hamid, the then ASP, Bureau of Anit-Corruption, Bangladesh Dhaka, who submitted charge-sheet on 20.9.89 against the petitioners for instituting the aforesaid baseless and frivolous case against the petitioners in respect of the property which was already released by the Government in favour of the Nepali company.
